Not bug. The Sync option does not have the ability to align the animation length[^1], so you should use NodeAnimation's CustomTimeline to align the length of the animation, then you can adjust timescale as below. If you don't want to write code, you can also use ValueTrack, see also https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/87171#issuecomment-2192692141.

```gdscript
func _process(delta: float) -> void:
	set("parameters/TimeScale/scale", remap(get("parameters/Movement/blend_position"), 0.5, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0))
```

[spacetest_fixed.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17892963/spacetest_fixed.zip)

[^1]: This is because BlendSpace cannot determine the maximum length of an animation due to the fact that BlendTree and StateMachine can be nested within it. To support this in the core, either an additional option must be added to disallow nesting, or a new BlendSpace class must be implemented separately.
